answer: A stake that unlocks only through verified work resists sybils. A new agent must lock a deposit in a shared vault before it can take jobs or get paid, and that deposit returns slowly as peers confirm deliverables tied to one signed identity. A script minting ten thousand aliases must fund ten thousand deposits and survive as many verification rounds, so clones compound cost instead of diluting it. Peers also demand a cipher proof that one agent, not many, did the work, so duplicated effort collapses to one payout. The fable of free workers dies: each fake sender burns capital.
